header: The small Luxon helpers for the places that used the built-in `Date` (step 65c). My rule (1 Nov 2026): "Luxon is the date and time library throughout the app; any other date or time handling is converted to Luxon". Luxon only: nothing here touches the built-in `Date` except where a caller hands one in (a database driver returns Dates). IST the plant's zone; "today" is the day in India, whatever zone the server (Vercel runs in UTC) or the visitor has. nowIso() the moment now as an ISO instant in UTC with milliseconds ("2026-11-01T10:00:00.000Z"): what `new Date().toISOString()` gave. toDateTime() a Date, a date string (ISO, SQL, RFC 2822, HTTP) or epoch milliseconds, as a DateTime (invalid when it is none of these). A date WITHOUT a time ("2026-02-05") is that calendar day, read in UTC, so that no zone can move it by a day (as `new Date("2026-02-05")` always was, a UTC midnight). toIsoInstant() the same as an ISO instant in UTC, or null when it is not a date.

symbols.name: toDateTime
symbols.sig: export function toDateTime(value: unknown, zone?: string): DateTime

behaviours: nowIso: an ISO instant in UTC with milliseconds, within two seconds of the clock
toIsoInstant(${v instanceof Date ? "Date " + v.toISOString() : JSON.stringify(v)}) equals new Date(...).toISOString() in zone ${ZONE}
a thing that is not a date gives null (the old code THREW a RangeError)
toDateTime: a Date, epoch milliseconds, a DateTime, strings with and without a time
a date WITHOUT a time is that calendar day, read in UTC, so no zone can move it
toDateTime does not turn rubbish into a date (a bare number string, words, an impossible day)
table cell ${v instanceof Date ? "Date " + v.toISOString() : JSON.stringify(v)}: Luxon equals the old text in zone ${ZONE}
table cells: an empty value is a dash, a value that is no date is shown as it is, a number and a text column are untouched
table cells: a September date reads 'Sept' (the British short month) exactly as before
'is it a real calendar day' (31.02 is none): Luxon and the old Date agree on every day-number of every month of 1900 to 2100
the number of days in each month of 1900 to 2100 (leap years included): the same
isSunday agrees with the old code for every real day of 2000 to 2100
parsePrintedDate keeps rejecting an impossible day and accepting the last day of a month (29.02.2024 yes, 29.02.2025 no, 31.04.2025 no)
the clock of the announcement form: the same text as before for 300 instants, in zone
DELIBERATE FIX: the date beside the clock is the day in INDIA (the old one printed the UTC day, so it was yesterday's date from midnight to 5:30 in the morning)
what the form sends to the server is the same instant in the same text as before
the PAX history and delegate dates: the same text as before for 300 instants (the old code used the visitor's zone, this is India's, as the editors are)
...the delegate's date alone ('31 Oct 2026')
the holiday toast ('8 Nov'): the same text as before for every day of 2026 and 2027's first days
the year of a published date: the same as before for Dates and timestamps (a date without a time is now its own year in every zone)
GUARD: no file of the program handles dates with the built-in Date (no new Date(, Date.parse, toLocaleDateString, getFullYear, Date.UTC); Luxon does
GUARD: no other date library is imported by the program (react-day-picker, a calendar WIDGET, is the only date package used, and only in two components, always with Luxon on the program's side of it)
the calendar widget is used in exactly the two components that were reviewed (each converts Luxon to a Date only at the widget's edge)
${f}: Luxon is imported, and the widget's Date is made by .toJSDate() and read back by DateTime.fromJSDate (the boundary)
